honesty: This is not a job guarantee. Nobody is hiring you because of a streak.
There is no certificate. The repos and the posts are the certificate.
Budget 45 minutes a night. Most people quit because they planned for ten.
It is free. There is no paid tier and no upsell at day 30.

howItWorks.title: Pick a track
howItWorks.body: Frontend, Backend, Data & ML, Mobile or DevOps. One track, 60 tasks, each sized for about 45 minutes.

howItWorks.title: Ship the proof, not the promise
howItWorks.body: Each day closes with two things: a commit on GitHub and a post on LinkedIn. We draft the post for you from what you actually built.

howItWorks.title: Become findable
howItWorks.body: Your build log becomes a public page. Recruiters search it by track, by stack, by consistency.

shelf.title: Toast queue with pause on hover

days.title: Ship one commit. Any size.
days.brief: Tonight only has to happen. The size of the commit is irrelevant.
days.why: Night one only has to happen. Everything else is built on the fact that you started.
days.build: Any repo, any commit. A single README counts.
doneWhen: A public repo exists with your name on it.
At least one commit is pushed.
The README says what you intend to build over 60 nights.
days.stretch: Add a plan for what you want to have built by day 60.
days.hint: Do not design tonight. Just push something and go to sleep.

days.title: A button that handles every state
days.brief: Default, hover, focus, active, disabled, loading. Six states, one component.
days.why: Six states is the difference between a button and a control people trust.
days.build: One Button component covering default, hover, focus, active, disabled and loading.
doneWhen: All six states are visibly distinct.
Focus is visible without a mouse.
Disabled cannot be clicked or tabbed into.
Loading keeps the button width steady.
days.stretch: Add a variant prop for primary, secondary and danger.
days.hint: Build the loading state first. It is the one that changes the layout.

days.title: Centre a div three different ways
days.brief: Flexbox, grid and absolute positioning. Know which one to reach for.
days.why: Knowing three ways means you pick the right one instead of the one you remember.
days.build: The same box centred with flexbox, with grid, and with absolute positioning.
doneWhen: All three are horizontally and vertically centred.
Each works when the box changes size.
You wrote a comment on when to use each.
days.stretch: Add a fourth using only margin auto and see where it fails.
days.hint: Try each one with a box whose height you do not know.

days.title: An input that validates as you type
days.brief: Feedback while typing, not after submitting. Do not shout at people mid-word.
days.why: Feedback after submitting is a punishment. Feedback while typing is help.
days.build: A text input that validates as the user types, without shouting mid-word.
doneWhen: No error shows until the field is left or clearly wrong.
The message says how to fix it, not just what failed.
Valid state is shown, not only invalid.
The error is announced to a screen reader.
days.stretch: Add a debounce so validation does not fire on every keystroke.
days.hint: Do not validate an email until it contains an at sign.

days.title: A responsive card grid with no media queries
days.brief: Let the grid do the work. Learn what auto-fit and minmax actually do.
days.why: Media queries are a blunt tool. The grid can do this by itself.
days.build: A card grid that reflows from one column to four with no breakpoints.
doneWhen: Reflows smoothly from 320px to 1400px.
No media queries in the CSS.
Cards keep a sensible minimum width.
Last row does not stretch oddly.
days.stretch: Make the first card span two columns when there is room.
days.hint: Look up grid-template-columns with repeat, auto-fit and minmax.

days.title: A loading skeleton that matches its content
days.brief: Same dimensions as the real thing, so nothing jumps when data arrives.
days.why: A spinner tells you nothing. A skeleton tells you what is coming.
days.build: A skeleton that matches the exact dimensions of the content it replaces.
doneWhen: Skeleton and content have identical height.
Nothing shifts when the real content arrives.
The shimmer respects reduced motion.
Screen readers announce loading, not the fake text.
days.stretch: Derive the skeleton from the real component so they cannot drift.
days.hint: Screenshot both states and flip between them. Any jump is a bug.

days.title: Dark mode with CSS variables
days.brief: One set of tokens, two themes, no duplicated stylesheet.
days.why: One set of tokens, two themes. Duplicating a stylesheet is how themes rot.
days.build: A dark mode built entirely on CSS custom properties.
doneWhen: One variable set, overridden in one place.
No duplicated colour values.
The choice survives a page refresh.
Both themes pass contrast checks.
days.stretch: Add a third theme in under five minutes to prove the structure works.
days.hint: If you are writing a colour twice, you need another variable.

days.title: An accessible dropdown, no library
days.brief: Arrow keys, escape to close, focus returns to the trigger.
days.why: Dropdowns are where accessibility usually dies quietly.
days.build: A select-style dropdown with no library.
doneWhen: Arrow keys move between options.
Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger.
Clicking outside closes it.
The trigger announces the selected value.
days.stretch: Add type-ahead so pressing a letter jumps to that option.
days.hint: Build it keyboard-first. Add the mouse afterwards.

days.title: Debounced search with cancel
days.brief: Stop firing a request on every keystroke, and cancel the ones in flight.
days.why: Firing a request per keystroke is how you get rate limited on day one.
days.build: A search box that debounces input and cancels requests in flight.
doneWhen: No request fires until typing pauses.
Older requests are cancelled, not just ignored.
Results never arrive out of order.
Clearing the box clears the results.
days.stretch: Show a subtle indicator while a request is in flight.
days.hint: AbortController is the piece most people skip.

days.title: An accessible modal, no library
days.brief: Focus trap, escape to close, background does not scroll.
days.why: A modal that traps focus badly is worse than no modal.
days.build: An accessible modal with no library.
doneWhen: Focus moves into the modal on open.
Tab cycles inside it and nowhere else.
Escape closes it and restores focus.
The page behind does not scroll.
days.stretch: Add a confirm variant that returns a promise.
days.hint: Store the element that had focus before opening. You need it on close.

days.title: A toast queue that pauses on hover
days.brief: Three toasts at once should stack, not overlap. Hovering should stop the timer.
days.why: Notifications are where beginners discover that timers and React state disagree.
days.build: A useToast hook and a Toaster component that can show up to three stacked messages.
doneWhen: Toasts stack rather than overlapping.
Hovering any toast pauses its dismiss timer.
Dismissing one does not reset the others.
A screen reader announces the message.
days.stretch: Add a swipe-to-dismiss gesture on touch devices.
days.hint: Store the remaining time, not the elapsed time. Pausing is then just declining to tick.

days.title: Make a component that survives bad data
days.brief: Build a profile card that renders correctly when the name, avatar and bio are all missing. Empty states are the whole task.
days.why: Real APIs return nulls. Most student portfolios break the moment a field is missing, and that is exactly what an interviewer will click on first.
days.build: A ProfileCard component that takes one user object and renders sensibly no matter what is inside it.
doneWhen: Missing avatar falls back to initials, never a broken image icon.
Missing name shows a neutral label, not "undefined".
Bio longer than 140 characters truncates without breaking layout.
Card holds its height across all four cases so the page does not jump.
Renders correctly at 390px wide.
days.stretch: Add a loading skeleton that matches the card's exact dimensions.
days.hint: Start from the worst case, not the best one. Write the component with an empty object first, then add fields back in.

Day 12 of 60.

Built a profile card that does not fall apart when the data is missing: no avatar, no name, no bio, still renders clean and holds its height.

Empty states are boring to build and obvious when they are absent. Learned that the hard way tonight.

React · #60DaysOfBuilding #ABTalks

Day 12 of 60.

Today's lesson: undefined is a design problem, not a bug. Built a profile card that stays intact with no avatar, no name and no bio.

Fallback initials, truncated bio, fixed height so nothing jumps.

React · #60DaysOfBuilding #ABTalks

Day 12 of 60.

Spent 45 minutes on empty states. A profile card that renders the same whether the API gives me everything or nothing.

Nobody notices this work until it is missing.

React · #60DaysOfBuilding #ABTalks

days.title: Infinite scroll that does not leak memory
days.brief: Load more as you scroll, and clean up after yourself when the component unmounts.
days.why: Every feed you have ever used does this, and almost every first attempt leaks an observer.
days.build: A list that loads the next page when a sentinel element enters the viewport.
doneWhen: New items load before the user hits the bottom.
The observer disconnects on unmount.
A loading row appears while fetching, not a full-page spinner.
Reaching the end shows an explicit end-of-list message.
days.stretch: Add a manual Load more button for people who use keyboards.
days.hint: IntersectionObserver on a sentinel div is simpler than listening to scroll events.

days.title: A date picker for one hand
days.brief: Assume a thumb, a 390px screen and no patience.
days.why: A date picker built for a mouse is unusable with a thumb.
days.build: A date picker sized for one hand on a 390px screen.
doneWhen: Every target is at least 44px.
Reachable in the lower half of the screen.
Month navigation needs one tap.
Typing a date still works.
days.stretch: Add quick options for today and tomorrow.
days.hint: Open it from the bottom of the screen, not the top.

days.title: Optimistic UI with rollback
days.brief: Show the result immediately, undo it cleanly when the request fails.
days.why: Waiting for a server before showing a result makes an app feel slow.
days.build: A like button that updates instantly and rolls back on failure.
doneWhen: The UI updates before the request resolves.
A failure reverts the change.
The user is told when a rollback happens.
Rapid clicks do not corrupt the count.
days.stretch: Queue changes while offline and replay them on reconnect.
days.hint: Keep the previous value. Rollback is just putting it back.

days.title: A virtualised list of 10,000 rows
days.brief: Render only what is visible. Learn why the DOM is the bottleneck.
days.why: Ten thousand DOM nodes is how a list becomes a slideshow.
days.build: A list of 10,000 rows that only renders what is visible.
doneWhen: Scrolling stays smooth throughout.
DOM node count stays roughly constant.
The scrollbar reflects the full list.
Keyboard scrolling still works.
days.stretch: Support rows of differing heights.
days.hint: Render a spacer with the full height, then position visible rows inside it.

days.title: Drag to reorder, keyboard accessible
days.brief: If it only works with a mouse, it does not work.
days.why: If it only works with a mouse, it does not work.
days.build: A reorderable list that works by drag and by keyboard.
doneWhen: Drag reorders with a clear drop indicator.
Arrow keys move the selected item.
Each move is announced to a screen reader.
The new order persists.
days.stretch: Add an undo for the last move.
days.hint: Build the keyboard version first. Dragging is the easier half.

days.title: A tab component that syncs to the URL
days.brief: Refreshing the page should keep the tab you were on.
days.why: A tab you cannot link to is a tab you cannot share.
days.build: A tab component whose state lives in the URL.
doneWhen: Refreshing keeps the current tab.
Back and forward move between tabs.
The URL is shareable.
Arrow keys move between tabs.
days.stretch: Add a default tab that does not pollute the URL.
days.hint: Use the query string. Hash fragments fight anchor links.

days.title: Copy to clipboard with real feedback
days.brief: The button text should change, and change back.
days.why: A copy button with no feedback makes people click it four times.
days.build: Copy to clipboard with feedback that resets itself.
doneWhen: Button text changes on success.
It resets after a couple of seconds.
Failure is handled, not silent.
The change is announced to a screen reader.
days.stretch: Copy formatted and plain text at once.
days.hint: The Clipboard API needs a user gesture and a secure context.

days.title: An image with a blur-up placeholder
days.brief: No layout shift, no white flash, works on a slow connection.
days.why: A white flash then a layout jump is the cheapest thing to fix and the most common.
days.build: An image with a blur-up placeholder and no layout shift.
doneWhen: Space is reserved before the image loads.
A blurred placeholder shows first.
Failure shows a real fallback.
Alt text is present and meaningful.
days.stretch: Add native lazy loading and measure the difference.
days.hint: Set width and height attributes. The aspect ratio does the rest.

days.title: A multi-step form that survives a refresh
days.brief: Losing four steps of input to an accidental reload is a design failure.
days.why: Losing four steps of typing to an accidental refresh is a design failure.
days.build: A multi-step form that survives a reload.
doneWhen: Progress restores after a refresh.
Back moves a step, not off the page.
Each step validates before advancing.
A completed submit clears the saved state.
days.stretch: Warn before leaving with unsaved changes.
days.hint: Save on change, not on step transition.

days.title: Empty, loading, error and success in one component
days.brief: Four states, one component, no copy-pasted markup.
days.why: Four states copy-pasted four times is four places to fix a bug.
days.build: One component that handles empty, loading, error and success.
doneWhen: All four render from one component.
Empty invites an action, it is not just a message.
Error says what happened and how to retry.
No duplicated markup between states.
days.stretch: Add a partial state for cached data being refreshed.
days.hint: Make the state an explicit value, not a mix of booleans.

days.title: A tooltip that never leaves the viewport
days.brief: Flip it when it would be cut off. Test it in the corner.
days.why: A tooltip clipped by the viewport is worse than no tooltip.
days.build: A tooltip that flips when it would be cut off.
doneWhen: Flips near any edge.
Never overflows the viewport.
Appears on focus, not only hover.
Escape dismisses it.
days.stretch: Add a small delay before showing, none before hiding.
days.hint: Test it in all four corners. That is where it breaks.

days.title: Client-side routing without a router
days.brief: Understand the History API before you let a library hide it.
days.why: Understand the History API before you let a library hide it.
days.build: Client-side routing in about 50 lines, no library.
doneWhen: Links change the view without a reload.
Back and forward work.
A direct URL loads the right view.
An unknown route shows a real 404.
days.stretch: Add a route parameter such as a user id.
days.hint: pushState plus a popstate listener is most of it.

days.title: Form validation that reads like a human
days.brief: Say what is wrong and how to fix it. Never just "invalid input".
days.why: Invalid input is not an error message. It is a shrug.
days.build: Validation messages a human can act on.
doneWhen: Every message says how to fix it.
No jargon and no error codes.
Messages sit next to their field.
Errors are announced, not only coloured.
days.stretch: Add a summary at the top that links to each bad field.
days.hint: Read each message aloud. If it sounds rude, rewrite it.

days.title: Undo and redo for a text field
days.brief: A small state machine, and your first taste of command patterns.
days.why: Undo is the feature that makes people brave.
days.build: Undo and redo for a text field.
doneWhen: Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z both work.
History has a sensible depth limit.
A new edit clears the redo stack.
Rapid typing groups into one step.
days.stretch: Add a visible history the user can jump into.
days.hint: Store snapshots, not diffs. Diffs are day 49.

days.title: A chart with no chart library
days.brief: SVG, some maths, and a lot less bundle weight.
days.why: A chart library is 200KB. Sometimes you need one line and some maths.
days.build: A line chart in raw SVG.
doneWhen: Scales correctly to its container.
Axes are labelled.
The data is available as a table for screen readers.
Works with 2 points and with 200.
days.stretch: Add a hover state showing the value at a point.
days.hint: Map your data range onto the pixel range. That is the whole trick.

days.title: Keyboard shortcuts that do not fight the browser
days.brief: Do not steal Ctrl+F. Learn which keys are yours.
days.why: Stealing Ctrl+F is how you make a user hate your app.
days.build: Keyboard shortcuts that respect the browser.
doneWhen: No browser shortcut is overridden.
Shortcuts do not fire while typing in an input.
A help overlay lists them.
They can be turned off.
days.stretch: Add a two-key sequence such as g then d.
days.hint: Check for an input or contenteditable target before acting.

days.title: A focus trap for an overlay
days.brief: Tab should cycle inside the overlay and nowhere else.
days.why: Focus escaping an overlay is the most common accessibility bug in production.
days.build: A reusable focus trap.
doneWhen: Tab and Shift+Tab stay inside.
Focus moves to the first sensible element on open.
Focus returns to the trigger on close.
Works with dynamically added elements.
days.stretch: Handle the case where the overlay has no focusable elements.
days.hint: Query focusable elements on each tab, not once on open.

days.title: Halfway. Refactor your day 12 card.
days.brief: Open the thing you built on day 12 and make it better. Note what you now see.
days.why: Halfway. The most useful thing you can do is look at your own old code.
days.build: Reopen day 12 and improve it with what you now know.
doneWhen: At least three specific improvements.
A written note on what you changed and why.
It still passes the original checklist.
The original version is still in your history.
days.stretch: Write the test you wish you had written on day 12.
days.hint: Do not rewrite it. Improve it. The difference matters.

days.title: File upload with drag, drop and progress
days.brief: Three states and a real progress number, not a fake spinner.
days.why: Upload is three states and a progress number, and most people fake all four.
days.build: A file upload with drag, drop and real progress.
doneWhen: Drag over shows a clear target.
Progress reflects actual bytes sent.
Failure offers a retry.
A file picker fallback exists.
days.stretch: Support multiple files with per-file progress.
days.hint: XMLHttpRequest still gives better upload progress than fetch.

days.title: Pagination that keeps scroll position
days.brief: Going back should not send the user to the top of the page.
days.why: Sending someone to the top of the page on every page change is a small cruelty.
days.build: Pagination that preserves scroll position.
doneWhen: Going back restores the previous position.
The page number is in the URL.
Loading does not collapse the layout.
Keyboard users can reach the controls.
days.stretch: Prefetch the next page on hover.
days.hint: Save the scroll offset before navigating, restore after render.

days.title: A search that highlights matches
days.brief: Highlight without breaking the markup or the accessibility tree.
days.why: Highlighting matches by string replacement breaks your markup.
days.build: Search results with highlighted matches.
doneWhen: Matches are highlighted safely, not by injecting HTML.
Case-insensitive matching works.
Special characters do not break it.
Highlighting does not confuse a screen reader.
days.stretch: Highlight multiple search terms in different colours.
days.hint: Split the string into parts and render them. Never set innerHTML.

days.title: Filter chips with a clear-all
days.brief: Multiple filters, visible state, one way out.
days.why: Filters with no visible state are filters people forget they applied.
days.build: Filter chips with a clear-all.
doneWhen: Active filters are obviously active.
Each chip removes individually.
Clear-all appears only when something is active.
The result count updates live.
days.stretch: Put the filter state in the URL so it can be shared.
days.hint: Show the count of results, not just the results.

days.title: A comment thread that nests three deep
days.brief: Recursion in components, and the point where indentation stops working on mobile.
days.why: Recursion in components is easy. Indentation on a 390px screen is not.
days.build: A comment thread nested three levels deep.
doneWhen: Renders recursively without duplicated code.
Readable at 390px at every depth.
Depth is capped with a continue-thread link.
Nesting is conveyed to screen readers.
days.stretch: Add collapse and expand per branch.
days.hint: Stop indenting after level two. Use a marker instead.

days.title: A sticky header that hides on scroll down
days.brief: Reveal on scroll up. Get the thresholds right or it feels broken.
days.why: Hide on scroll down, reveal on scroll up. Get the threshold wrong and it feels broken.
days.build: A sticky header that hides and reveals.
doneWhen: Hides on scroll down, reveals on scroll up.
Does not flicker on small movements.
Always visible at the top of the page.
Respects reduced motion.
days.stretch: Add a shadow only once the page has scrolled.
days.hint: Use a threshold of about 10 pixels. Anything less flickers.

days.title: Skeleton to content with no layout shift
days.brief: Measure your CLS before and after. Numbers, not vibes.
days.why: Cumulative layout shift is measurable. Fix it with numbers, not vibes.
days.build: A skeleton to content transition with zero shift.
doneWhen: Measured CLS is under 0.1.
Nothing moves when content arrives.
Before and after numbers are recorded.
Images have reserved space.
days.stretch: Add a font loading strategy that avoids text reflow.
days.hint: Chrome DevTools has a layout shift overlay. Turn it on.

days.title: A settings page that saves on change
days.brief: No save button. Show what saved and when.
days.why: A save button is a question the user should not have to answer.
days.build: A settings page that saves as you change things.
doneWhen: Changes save without a button.
A saved indicator appears and fades.
Failure is visible and retryable.
Rapid changes do not race.
days.stretch: Add an undo for the last change.
days.hint: Debounce the save, but show the pending state immediately.

days.title: An offline banner and a retry queue
days.brief: Patchy 4G is the default condition, not the edge case.
days.why: Patchy 4G is the default condition for your users, not an edge case.
days.build: An offline banner with a retry queue.
doneWhen: A banner appears when the connection drops.
Actions queue instead of failing.
The queue replays on reconnect.
The user can see what is pending.
days.stretch: Persist the queue so it survives a refresh.
days.hint: The online and offline events lie sometimes. Verify with a real request.

days.title: A stepper that shows real progress
days.brief: Steps behind, current step, steps ahead. Honest about what remains.
days.why: A progress bar that does not reflect reality is worse than none.
days.build: A stepper showing real progress through a flow.
doneWhen: Completed, current and upcoming steps are distinct.
Completed steps can be revisited.
Progress is announced to screen readers.
Fits five steps at 390px.
days.stretch: Allow skipping optional steps and show that clearly.
days.hint: Show the step name, not just a number.

days.title: A sortable table with a mobile fallback
days.brief: Tables do not fit at 390px. Decide what they become instead.
days.why: Tables do not fit at 390px. Decide what yours becomes instead.
days.build: A sortable table with a real mobile layout.
doneWhen: Sorts by any column, both directions.
Becomes cards or a list below 640px.
Sort state is announced.
Sorting is stable.
days.stretch: Add multi-column sorting.
days.hint: Do not just scroll it sideways. Change the shape.

days.title: A password field with honest strength feedback
days.brief: Say what would make it stronger, not just "weak".
days.why: Weak is not feedback. Say what would make it stronger.
days.build: A password field with honest strength feedback.
doneWhen: Feedback names the specific improvement.
No arbitrary character rules.
A visibility toggle exists.
Strength is announced, not only coloured.
days.stretch: Check against a list of common passwords.
days.hint: Length beats complexity. Say so.

days.title: A carousel that works with swipe and keyboard
days.brief: The most-hated component on the web. Build a good one.
days.why: The most-hated component on the web. Build a good one.
days.build: A carousel that works by swipe and by keyboard.
doneWhen: Swipe works on touch.
Arrow keys work.
Current position is visible.
Autoplay pauses on focus and hover.
days.stretch: Add a reduced-motion variant with no sliding.
days.hint: Scroll snap gets you most of the way with far less code.

days.title: Toast, modal and focus, all together
days.brief: Three things you have built separately, now competing for the same focus.
days.why: Three things you built separately, now fighting over the same focus.
days.build: A modal that opens a toast and returns focus correctly.
doneWhen: Toast is announced while the modal is open.
Closing the modal returns focus correctly.
Toast does not steal focus.
Escape closes only the top layer.
days.stretch: Add a confirm dialog opened from inside the modal.
days.hint: Keep a stack of layers. The top one owns escape.

days.title: Rate limit feedback a user understands
days.brief: Not "429". Say how long to wait and why.
days.why: 429 is not an error message. It is a status code.
days.build: Rate limit feedback a person understands.
doneWhen: Says how long to wait.
Explains why in plain words.
A countdown updates live.
Retry is disabled until it is useful.
days.stretch: Retry automatically with backoff once the wait ends.
days.hint: Read the Retry-After header. It is usually there.

days.title: A calendar month view at 390px
days.brief: Seven columns on a narrow screen. Something has to give.
days.why: Seven columns on a 390px screen. Something has to give.
days.build: A month calendar that works at 390px.
doneWhen: All seven columns fit with no horizontal scroll.
Today is clearly marked.
Arrow keys move by day.
Days with events are distinguishable.
days.stretch: Add a swipe gesture to change month.
days.hint: Drop the day names to single letters below 400px.

days.title: A bottom sheet with drag to dismiss
days.brief: The mobile pattern people actually reach for.
days.why: The pattern mobile users actually reach for.
days.build: A bottom sheet with drag to dismiss.
doneWhen: Drags down to dismiss with a threshold.
Snaps back if not dragged far enough.
A backdrop tap closes it.
Focus is trapped while open.
days.stretch: Add a half-open detent.
days.hint: Track velocity, not only distance. A fast flick should close it.

days.title: A command palette with fuzzy search
days.brief: Cmd+K. Keyboard-first, and it should feel instant.
days.why: Cmd+K. Keyboard-first, and it has to feel instant.
days.build: A command palette with fuzzy search.
doneWhen: Opens with a shortcut from anywhere.
Fuzzy matching, not exact substring.
Arrow keys and Enter select.
Feels instant with 500 commands.
days.stretch: Add recent commands at the top.
days.hint: Score matches by consecutive character runs.

days.title: A diff view for two strings
days.brief: Show what changed, character by character.
days.why: Show what changed, not that something changed.
days.build: A character-level diff of two strings.
doneWhen: Additions and deletions are visually distinct.
Handles multi-line input.
Colour is not the only signal.
Performs acceptably on long text.
days.stretch: Add a word-level mode alongside character-level.
days.hint: Longest common subsequence is the classic approach. Start small.

days.title: Animate a list add and remove
days.brief: Items should not pop in and out. Respect reduced motion.
days.why: Items popping in and out makes a list feel broken.
days.build: Animated add and remove on a list.
doneWhen: Additions animate in.
Removals animate out before disappearing.
Surrounding items move smoothly.
Reduced motion disables all of it.
days.stretch: Animate reordering as well as add and remove.
days.hint: Measure positions before and after, then animate the difference.

days.title: A form that tells you what changed
days.brief: Highlight dirty fields and warn before discarding them.
days.why: A form that discards your work without asking has broken a promise.
days.build: A form that shows what changed.
doneWhen: Changed fields are visibly marked.
A count of changes is shown.
Discard asks first.
Reset returns to the original values.
days.stretch: Add a per-field revert.
days.hint: Keep the initial values. Everything else is a comparison.

days.title: A print stylesheet for a receipt
days.brief: Nobody does this. It takes 30 minutes and it always impresses.
days.why: Nobody does this. It takes 30 minutes and it always impresses.
days.build: A print stylesheet for a receipt.
doneWhen: Prints cleanly to A4.
Navigation and buttons are hidden.
Content does not break across pages badly.
Link URLs are shown in the printed output.
days.stretch: Add a page header and footer with page numbers.
days.hint: Use the print preview constantly. It is the only real test.

days.title: An error boundary that is actually useful
days.brief: Tell the user what broke and give them a way forward.
days.why: Something went wrong is not help. It is an apology with no content.
days.build: An error boundary that gives the user a way forward.
doneWhen: Catches render errors without a white screen.
Offers a specific next action.
Logs enough detail to debug.
The rest of the app still works.
days.stretch: Add a reset that retries without a full reload.
days.hint: Per-section boundaries beat one at the root.

days.title: A theme switcher that respects system preference
days.brief: Three states: light, dark, and whatever the system says.
days.why: Three states, not two. The third is what the system already said.
days.build: A theme switcher with light, dark and system.
doneWhen: All three options work.
System follows OS changes live.
The choice persists.
No flash of the wrong theme on load.
days.stretch: Add a smooth transition that respects reduced motion.
days.hint: An inline script before paint prevents the flash.

days.title: Reduce your bundle by 30 percent
days.brief: Measure first. Then delete something.
days.why: Measure first. Then delete something.
days.build: A 30 percent bundle reduction on a real page.
doneWhen: Before and after sizes are recorded.
The reduction is at least 30 percent.
Nothing broke.
You can name what caused the win.
days.stretch: Set a bundle size budget that fails the build.
days.hint: One oversized dependency is usually most of it. Find it first.

days.title: Audit one page for accessibility
days.brief: Keyboard only, then screen reader. Write down every failure.
days.why: Keyboard only, then a screen reader. Write down every failure.
days.build: A full accessibility audit of one page.
doneWhen: Whole page usable by keyboard alone.
Tested with a real screen reader.
Every failure written down.
At least three are fixed.
days.stretch: Add an automated check to your build.
days.hint: Unplug the mouse. That is the whole first half of the audit.

days.title: A profile page built from your own build log
days.brief: Use your 56 days of commits as the data source.
days.why: Fifty-six nights of commits is a dataset. Use it.
days.build: A profile page built from your own build log.
doneWhen: Reads from your real commit history.
Shows the streak and the artifacts.
Works at 390px.
Loads in under two seconds.
days.stretch: Add a filter by track or by technology.
days.hint: The GitHub API gives you commits per repo without authentication.

days.title: A landing page for the thing you built
days.brief: Explain your best project to someone who has never seen it.
days.why: Explain your best project to someone who has never seen it.
days.build: A landing page for the thing you are proudest of.
doneWhen: A stranger understands it in ten seconds.
Shows the thing working, not only describing it.
One clear call to action.
Works at 390px.
days.stretch: Add a 30 second demo recording.
days.hint: Lead with what it does. Save how it works for later.

days.title: Write the README you wish you had
days.brief: Go back to day 1 and document it properly.
days.why: Go back to night one and document it properly.
days.build: The README you wish day 1 had.
doneWhen: Explains what it is and why it exists.
Setup instructions someone can actually follow.
A screenshot or a recording.
Honest about what is unfinished.
days.stretch: Add a short architecture note.
days.hint: Ask someone to follow your setup steps exactly. Watch where they stop.

days.title: Ship your build log and post the recap
days.brief: Sixty repos, one page, one honest post about what changed.
days.why: Sixty repos, one page, one honest post about what changed.
days.build: Your public build log and the recap post.
doneWhen: All 60 days are on one page.
Links to every repo work.
The recap is honest about the nights you missed.
The page works at 390px.
days.stretch: Add what you would tell yourself on night one.
days.hint: Write the post you would have believed on day 1.
